body.h1: RECEPTIVITY OF AN ENDOMETRIUM FOR EMBRYONIC

h1.u: RENEWED PETITION TO ACCEPT COLOR DRAWINGS

body.p: In response to the Decision on the Petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.84(a)(2) dated August 24, 2021, applicant files this renewed petition requesting that the Office accept color drawings in the present application.

The subject matter of the invention relates to methods and kits for determining receptivity status of an endometrium for embryonic implantation. The color drawing in FIG 1 is necessary to accurately and clearly depict the subject matter sought to be patented. Applicant provides a detailed description as to why the color in FIG. 1 is necessary.

FIG. 1. depicts a Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING) v.10.0 database generated protein interaction network of proteins codified by 184 window of implantation (WOI) selected genes related to endometrial receptivity and embryonic implantation. FIG. 1 shows a total of 1,334 predicted protein-protein interactions for the set of 184 WO1 genes. FIG1. 1 has colored nodes and eight (8) differently colored lines. Each node represents a protein. Colored nodes depict query proteins and "first shell of interactions" (i.e., proteins that directly associated with the 184 proteins), and clear white nodes represent "second shell of interactions" (i.e., indirect protein interactions between the 184 proteins). Each colored line represents a different type of evidence that was used in order to predict a protein interaction between two proteins. For example, red lines represent the presence of gene fusion evidence; green lines represent gene neighborhood evidence; blue lines represent gene co-occurrence evidence (i.e., protein interactions that are conserved in the species); magenta lines represent experimentally determined evidence (i.e., protein interactions that were experimentally gathered Application No. : 17/146,619

Page : 2of5 from other protein-protein interaction databases); yellow lines represent textmining evidence (i.e., protein interactions that were extracted from the titles and abstracts of scientific literature); turquoise lines represent curated database evidence (i.e., protein interactions that were gathered from curated databases, e.g., Biocarta, BioCyc, GO, KEGG, and Reactome); black lines represent coexpression evidence (i.e., genes that are co-expressed in the same or in other species); and lavender lines represent protein homology evidence. The predicted protein-protein interactions are important because the total number of predicted protein-protein interactions is far greater than was expected in the network analysis, and greater than would be expected for a random set of proteins of similar size. The data in FIG.1 shows that these 184 proteins were biologically connected as a group. Such extensive protein-protein interactions cannot be clearly conveyed in a black and white image. As demonstrated below, applicant provides Color and Grayscale images for FIG. 1 below, with arrows and symbols overlaid to simplify applicant's argument. If the image is converted to grayscale, information regarding the type of protein-protein interaction is lost.

As shown in the images below, the line depicted by the arrow with asterisks "*" in color FIG. 1 is clearly distinguishable (magenta) from the line near the arrow with the symbol "A" (turquoise), and the line near the arrow (green). This distinction between the colored lines depicted by the three arrows types is not clear in the grayscale version of FIG. 1. This is not ideal for a reader trying to understand the invention of the application, especially when looking for the type of protein-protein interaction. Thus, a color drawing for FIG. 1 is the only practical medium by which to disclose the subject matter sought to be patented.

In view of the foregoing, applicant requests that the Office reconsider its decision denying the petition for color drawings. Based on the explanation provided above for at least one figure (FIG. 1), applicant submits that the color drawings should be accepted.

To clearly meet the requirements of 37 CFR 1.84(2)(ii), one set of the color drawings is being submitted together with this application via the Electronic Filing System. These drawings are identical to the figures originally filed with the application on January 12, 2021.

The fees in the amount of $140 cover the required fee under 37 C.F.R. § 1.17(h) are being transmitted with this request via the Electronic Filing System. Applicant includes a courtesy copy of the color drawings and notes that one (1) set of the color drawings and reference to the color drawings in the specification as required under 37 C.F.R § 1.84(a)(2) were filed in this application on January 12, 2021.
